_about: Units decide's quality store and the figures its land rules read (the design director's ruling of 24 November 2026 15:53Z on rules-builder/release2/soviet/form.md, the #2 form, with Part 2's one store for soldiers, pilots and crews). Read only in a grand campaign opened with Units decide (src/campaign/units.ts); off, nothing here is read. One rule for every nation: a nation named here is a seed or a start row, never a rule. Marks as the form uses them: F firm, L likely, D derived from read figures, M from memory, G the rules builder's guess, waiting on the measure, U not laid (the slot exists and nothing reads it).
_startRows: Rows a nation holds on the first day under Units decide only, never in tech.json 'start' (form, 'Where it goes'): Germany holds Field radios (it holds Staff colleges, tech.json start), and no other nation does; Sweden and Norway hold Winter equipment, so that holding it can stand in for the hardy list (east.json) at its three reads (Part 1 section 1; SOV and FIN already hold it). Applied by startOpen before the opening research (tech.ts openUnitsRows), so a later start's catch-up counts each row once. G.

land._ladder: Training is the ladder (ruling 15:53Z (4)): an army's level is the higher of its start seed (land.train) and this rung for one, two or three of the training rows held, the same ladder for every nation. A start never fixes a ceiling. 1.25 is Germany's level (nations.json). G.
land._trainRows: The training rows the ladder counts, held live from the tree (Part 1 2a): NCO schools, Battle drill, Officer schools. Each has no other effect. G.
land._radios: Command c = this if the nation holds the row, plus earned, at most 1 (Part 1 2b). Staff colleges, Battle groups and Deep operations keep their one price in techMul and never feed c (choice 15). G.
land._earned: Command earned in war, 0 to 1 (Part 1 2b). seed: the start's c by army, as the design director ruled at 24 Nov 16:06Z (round-2-build-order.md:2159; the form's 'Seeds ruled 16:07Z' under ruling 15:53Z (5)) on the historian's reading of command and signals 1939-41 (historian/prisoners-command-1124.md Part 2, scores D): GER 1, SOV 0 and FRA 0, held (L); POL 0.1 (F/L); ITA 0.25 (L); JAP 0.5 (L); UK 0.5 (F/L); USA 0.5, the range middle, its score leaning on memory until the 1941 manoeuvres are read (M); '_default' 0.5, the range middle, for every army the historian has not read, marked as a stand-in until it is read, never today's 1 (G). No seed is shaved to steer a gate: UK, USA and JAP pass the blitz gate once they research radios (0.5 + 0.15 = 0.65), and that is the cause working. The store holds the seed less 'radios' where the row is held at the start (so GER 0.85), never below 0. The same at every start month: history plays a later start's months with the switch off, and the 1941-42 rises come from the earned test and the radios row in play, never from dates (G). month: added for each month the nation's own attacks take at least 'provinces' provinces from an enemy (one test on the month's battle reports, the player's nation and every computer's alike; sieges, reliefs and sallies left out; a walk-in after the defenders yielded counts; distinct regions). corps: taken off for each corps taken whole (cut off, rule 232, a cut road). All G.
land._attack: Attack is multiplied by base + perC x c, in place of slowCommand's x0.85 (Part 1 2b): at c 0 today's slow command, at c 1 none. G.
land._mostCorps: Most corps one battle can take: base + perC x c, in place of maxAttack (Part 1 2b; choice 11): 8 at c 0 (today's slow command), 20 at c 1. G.
land._gates: Command gates (Part 1 section 1): below 'renewal' a staff renews no failed attack and counter-attacks late (today's slowCommand habits); from 'blitz', with Field radios held, the tempo x1.2, the +1 move, the opening thrust and the armoured spearheads' x1.15, for any nation. G.
land._blitzTraits: The national trait rows the blitz gate stands in for (Part 1 section 1; Part 2 section 4 'Inert'): under the switch no nation's own row of them is read (traits.json). Their effects go instead to any nation through the gate: the tempo's x1.2 and +1 move by the fresh offensive, and the armoured spearheads' attack at the trait's own figure in traits.json, so each is priced once. Ids, no figure.
land._reforms: History's reforms of an army (diplomacy.json 'reform'; Part 1 section 1; choice 8): under the switch no reform writes the parts listed in 'land' (training, a slow command, the most corps), which are the army's own causes. Their other parts (the air) are applied on history's calendar as before, for the air thread to rule on. 'news': the reforms whose text is told once, as news, when a cause of the army each names passes a mark, never on the calendar: red-army-1943 when that army's command c reaches 0.5, german-army-1944 when that army's mean corps experience, having stood at 0.5 or more at a month's end, falls under 0.5 (the event's own conditions must hold). A mark is passed only from the other side of it, so an army that starts past one is not told it. Each is recorded in the store's news so it is told once. The other two (allied-armies-1944, italy-loses-heart) keep their calendar and tell their text there, without their land parts. G.
land._sight: A staff's sight s = clamp((c - from) / span, 0, 1) (Part 1 section 5). Seen odds = card odds x (q / wk)^(s - 1): at s 0 a staff counts men, kinds and ground, at s 1 it reads the card as today's staff does. The player's card shows the odds as the player's own staff reads them at the player's own sight (ruling 15:53Z (14)). G.
land._byOrders: The way 'mass', by orders (Part 1 section 5; ruling 15:53Z (1)): ordinary attacks go in at seen odds 'need' and stop adding corps at 'stop'; attacks in the main effort's sector keep today's stop, 'main' (ai.ts). As sight rises, need blends to the temper's minOdds and stop to 'main'. The doctrine's own content, never refit to Lawrence's 1.42, which is a check. Methodical, bold and night keep today's thresholds. G.
land._card: The words of the attack card's lines on the causes each side's staff reads (#2 form 'On the card'; Part 2 section 5; ruling 15:53Z (14) amended), for the UI director to change: never a flag or a date. training: the army's training level's word, the first whose 'below' it is under, else 'top'; 'seed' names an army whose level is its own start (no training row lifts it); the rows held are named as the research tree names them. command: the same for command c; 'radios' the radios row held and not held; 'carried' the months the army has carried an offensive through, for none, one and more ({n} the count). 'commandEffect': what the attacker's command does to this attack ({attack}, from 'attackDown' with {pct} or 'attackWhole') and the most corps it brings ({most}). ways: each land way's name on the card. sight: the sentence the player's card says where the player's own staff reads the odds at a sight under 1, 'none' at 0 and 'part' between, {command} the command line's words. The marks between the words are G: they wait on the UI director.

card.commandEffect: {attack}; at most {most} corps in one battle. It grows with each offensive carried through and falls with each corps taken whole
card.attackWhole: The attack goes in at full weight

sight.none: Your staff counts men, kinds and ground. Its command, {command}, cannot weigh the troops' worth or the enemy's works, and these odds leave both out.
sight.part: Your staff weighs the troops' worth and the enemy's works only in part, its command being {command}: these odds are its own reckoning.

land._xp: Corps experience by result, each times (1 - xp) (Part 1 2d), in place of today's flat +0.05 attacking and +0.04 defending, win or lose: the attacker that wins, the attacker repulsed, the defender that holds, the defender beaten. Drafts dilute every nation's corps. G.
land._label: Captured: of the defender's men lost, share x (attacker's per-man attack worth / defender's per-man defence worth) are booked as prisoners, at most 'cap' (Part 1 section 7). A split of men already lost; it adds none and goes in its own report field. D: fit to the record's fail-or-advance pair at Kursk (F, p. 34), 0.147 and 0.149.
land._guards: The Guards title, as a name only, in its own corps field (Part 1 section 1; Part 2 section 4; choice 13): a corps of any nation at xp at least 'xp' with at least 'taken' provinces taken (its record's 'taken': attacks won and ground walked into after the defenders gave way) takes it, the month it is earned, and its card and name carry the word its nation gives such a formation (stories.json designation). Never c.elite, so it adds nothing to the corps' worth: corpsBase's 0.85 + 0.4 xp already prices that experience. 'elite': the special formations (traits.json 'unit' ids) the earned title stands in for: under the switch none is bought (whyNoElite refuses it) and none adds its own edge in battle (the Soviet Guards corps' x1.15 would price experience twice). G.
land._raisedBy: Special formations raised by a research row in place of their first year (traits.json 'from'; Part 1 section 1; choice 13): the heavy tank corps needs Heavy tanks, and stays the nation's own unit as traits.json lists it until audit #4 replaces the units by nation. By traits.json 'unit' id, never by nation.
land._antiTank: The infantry's own anti-tank guns by the rows the defender's nation holds, in place of the calendar (Part 1 section 1): the year of support.json's antiTank.byYear row a defence takes, by how many of 'rows' its nation holds in order: none, the 1939 row; Anti-tank guns, the 1941 row; Anti-tank guns and Tank destroyers, the 1943 row. No new row. The row itself prices a nation without the research, so support.json's 'without' is not read on top of it; Tank destroyers' own share (support.json tankDestroyers) is read as before. The attacker's armour step (support.json armourStep) is measured against the tanks of the same year, the tanks the defence's guns were built to stop (support.ts armourOfTheDay of that year, weighed as the guns are), never the calendar's: nothing reads the year. G.
land._ways: The land ways a staff may hold (Part 2 section 3; data/battle/lean.json). Night and last-stand are fought as bold (lean.json standIn) until they are built.
land._school: The drafts' schools: 0 for every nation at every start month, as g.stories.schools holds today (Part 2 section 2). Under the switch it replaces g.stories.schools as the count the drafts' training and a new corps' experience read (stories.json veterans: green + perSchool x school, raised + perSchool x school), for every nation's corps. Raised by a schools order: the player's honours of the army and holders of the highest award from the army sent home as instructors (stories.ts, valour.ts), to veterans.maxSchools. An airman's school step is the air arm's (air.school, its size U), never the land's. A computer staff's schools order is not laid (U). G.

_trainIn: Months a change of way takes to train in, one time for every arm (Part 2 section 3). U until the historian reads one; the form's guess is 6 (G).

air._scale: One curve from a pilot's hours to a level, the same for every nation (Part 2 section 1). U: not laid; until it is, every group keeps its held level.
air._school: Hours before first combat a new pilot leaves school with, by start turn (Part 2 section 2; historian/air-reads-1124.md A). GER about 250 before the cuts (L; the reading dates no cut, so every offered start, 1939-42, takes it: G). RAF and US 350 and 400 are 1944 readings, so null; JAP (land) and SOV not read, null. A nation not listed is null: not laid (no '_default').
air._deck: The same for carrier pilots, kept apart: JAP 500 or more (the navy's carrier school before 1937, F). Others null. By start turn.
air._fighter: Fighter doctrines (fighters.ts) and escort doctrines (plan D). No start row is read, so every nation's slot is null (Part 2 section 2).

sea._ways: The fleet staff's ways (battle/sea/types.ts). No 'night' way: lean.json's night is seeded as its stand-in, bold (Part 2 section 2).
sea._pack: Convoy doctrine, by start turn, from the record (Part 2 section 2; naval-battles/wolfpack-r2/form.md:47-49): 1939 and 1940 every navy hunts alone; 1941 GER and ITA homed from ashore; 1942 GER homed; '_default' is every other navy. L.
sea._target: Boats go for warships first: JAP (wolfpack form :47); '_default', every other navy, merchants first. L.
